reference: No GNU doas CLI is available as an independent command oracle. Runnable expectations use Bash's documented type/help builtin behavior; the doas help bytes are transcribed from the static public builtin documentation in the implementation source, not sampled from the candidate. Privilege and delegation operations have no runnable oracle in this safe suite and are explicitly deferred.
coverage: Bash identifies doas as a builtin through type -t.
Bash help can resolve the loadable's documentation entry.
The doas --help and -h metadata paths return the declared usage text and success status.
exclusions: There is no matching GNU doas executable for command parity.
No doas operation is invoked: privilege transitions, authority ioctls, external command delegation, and command execution require a disposable VM or purpose-built mock.
This suite does not cover sudo, su, sudoedit, or any other loadable.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash's type -t builtin metadata reports the loaded doas command as a builtin.
Confirm Bash help recognizes the doas builtin documentation entry; the marker is printed only after help succeeds.
Check both documented doas help spellings return success and print the declared builtin usage text byte-for-byte.
cases.stdout:
doas - conservative doas front-end
usage: doas [-n] [-u USER] [-g GROUP] [-s] [--] command [args...]
       doas -L
Supports -g/--group as an explicit runas group when policy permits it.
Non-root callers use v2 authority when available, otherwise external doas.
Root callers drop and exec with scrubbed environment and child hygiene.

cases.purpose: Exercise non-root allow, deny, non-interactive deny, and interactive verification behavior at the authority boundary.
cases.reason: All obligations depend on guest /dev/bashos-auth v2 UAPI implementation (kernel module or a root-owned CUSE character-device mock implementing loadables/common/_bashos_auth_uapi.h: VERSION, PRIVCMD_AUTHZ, EXEC_VERIFY, EXEC_HANDOFF, token mint/consume, secret slots, policy info). The Debian guest kernel has no such device and the repository holds only the UAPI header, so open() fails with ENOENT and no unprivileged fixture can observe any ioctl behaviour. Without it the builtin routes to the external delegate (separate topic).

cases.purpose: Check the no-authority fallback's doas argv translation, status propagation, environment refresh, and descriptor cleanup.
cases.reason: The fallback is unprivileged and observable with a private delegate script; the original deferral to a privileged VM is unnecessary.

cases.purpose: Verify root-route target uid/gid selection, explicit group membership handling, and the resulting child identity.
cases.reason: The root route needs no authority device (doas.c bda_run_root) but needs euid 0 with private /etc/passwd and /etc/group: guest case option to run a side as uid 0 inside a private mount namespace with fixture /etc/passwd and /etc/group bind-mounted (guest.py terminal.child_limits always drops to uid 2000; a drop to a second synthetic uid needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID, the legacy runner disables user namespaces, and an unprivileged user namespace maps only one uid).

cases.purpose: Verify command arguments remain literal and the child receives the documented scrubbed environment, closed inherited descriptors, and command status.
cases.reason: The scrubbed-environment contract applies on the root route (guest case option to run a side as uid 0 inside a private mount namespace with fixture /etc/passwd and /etc/group bind-mounted (guest.py terminal.child_limits always drops to uid 2000; a drop to a second synthetic uid needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID, the legacy runner disables user namespaces, and an unprivileged user namespace maps only one uid)) and the authority route (guest /dev/bashos-auth v2 UAPI implementation (kernel module or a root-owned CUSE character-device mock implementing loadables/common/_bashos_auth_uapi.h: VERSION, PRIVCMD_AUTHZ, EXEC_VERIFY, EXEC_HANDOFF, token mint/consume, secret slots, policy info). The Debian guest kernel has no such device and the repository holds only the UAPI header, so open() fails with ENOENT and no unprivileged fixture can observe any ioctl behaviour). Literal argv, fd closure and status propagation are separately observable on the unprivileged delegate route (see external_delegate_fallback), which does not scrub the environment.
